name: Maternal feminism
summary: Maternal feminism held that women's roles as mothers and caregivers gave them a distinct moral authority and a duty to take part in public life. Its adherents campaigned for the vote, temperance, child and maternal welfare, health and sanitation, framing politics as 'municipal housekeeping' or enlarged motherhood. It accepted differences between the sexes and usually family-centred roles, and many strands were evangelical, pacifist before 1914, and sometimes tied to eugenic or imperial 'mothers of the race' ideas.
scope: The Anglo-American and British Empire movement from the late nineteenth century to the 1920s, especially Canada: Nellie McClung and the Famous Five, Jane Addams's municipal housekeeping argument, the WCTU and National Council of Women, with Ellen Key's Swedish motherhood-centred feminism as a continental parallel. It excludes later maternal-thinking and ethic-of-care philosophy (Ruddick, Gilligan) and equal-rights feminism that denied sex differences.

sources.author: Prairie Forum (University of Alberta journals)
sources.usedFor: Prairie maternal feminists' health and child-welfare demands, British-Canadian renewal themes and exclusions (abstract page read).

universal-healthcare.rationale: Prairie maternal feminists pressed hard for public health and medical care for mothers and children, so a state guarantee fits their aims.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from concern for working women and girls (Addams on young factory workers); no wage-floor argument is documented.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Inferred: the movement's reform case rests on public regulation, not market allocation; markets are barely discussed in the sources.

public-ownership.rationale: Socialist maternal feminists backed public ownership while liberal ones did not, and the sources do not settle it.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not discussed; strand split between well-to-do reformers and socialist maternal feminists, so no firm lean can be inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from concern for working women; socialist strands were pro-union but the mainstream's own texts say little.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred: reformers accepted regulation of tenements, food and sweatshops over owners' wishes (Addams).

regulate-corporations.rationale: Addams wants city inspection of sweatshops, food and housing, and McClung blames the liquor trade, so regulating business is routine for them.

cut-welfare.rationale: Maternal feminists built the case for mothers' and children's welfare provision, so cutting it contradicts their core aim.

worker-ownership.rationale: Only the socialist wing (Richardson, Henderson) would agree; the mainstream is silent.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not an issue the movement addressed and no principle clearly decides it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the temperance and moral-purity campaigns against intoxicants; drugs beyond alcohol were not their topic.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources indicates a position.

strong-leader.rationale: Inferred from their faith in democratic participation and the ballot (McClung, Addams); bypassing gridlock is not discussed.

state-harmful.rationale: They looked to city and state action (inspection, schools, health) to protect homes, which is the opposite of calling the state harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from their pacifism and protective concern for homes and children; guns were not a documented campaign.

empower-police-military.rationale: McClung attacks militarism and its hold on children and churches; more military power runs against that.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Moral-reform strands such as the Female Moral Reform Society and Pappritz opposed prostitution as exploitation of women.

decide-locally.rationale: Municipal housekeeping stressed city government, but they also sought national laws (child labor, votes); split.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from reformist, child-protective outlook; Hannah-Moffat links maternal reformers to women's prison reform, but not read in detail.

traditional-family.rationale: Wikipedia notes critics say the movement accepted existing sex roles and kept the family at the centre; they differ from traditionalists in wanting women public voice.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the family-centred, Protestant moral outlook of the movement.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred: 'mothers of the race' and moral-reform concerns made most oppose abortion, though Key backed fuller freedom in motherhood decisions.

more-religion-public.rationale: Evangelical Protestantism was central to the movement and the WCTU; McClung reads faith as a call to act in public.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The movement is documented as racially exclusionary and imperial; its own texts did not propose redress, so a low-confidence lean against.

gender-social-construct.rationale: They held that women are by nature nurturing and different from men, so gender is not mainly constructed.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Prairie and imperial strands wanted to renew the British-Canadian population and its culture through mothers.

gradual-change.rationale: They sought sweeping reform (suffrage, prohibition) but chose to work within existing roles and institutions; split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Racial undertones toward new immigrants existed, yet Addams defends immigrant women; no consistent position.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Pacifists hoped women's involvement would end war, but no documented view on international bodies.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred from pacifist internationalism of Stowe-Gullen and McClung, though imperial 'mothers of the race' talk pulled the other way.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from their pacifism; McClung says war is not of God's making.

open-borders.rationale: Concern about the birth rate and race of the nation counted against open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing suggests they would limit growth.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; reform relied on public action rather than technology.

revolution-justified.rationale: They pursued reform by the ballot and moral persuasion; McClung's weapon is the vote and a 'fair deal'.

experts-over-public.rationale: Addams values inspectors and officials but also demands women's votes; split.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred; only the socialist fringe would favour it.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed outside the socialist strand.

land-value-tax.rationale: Single-tax land reform appears nowhere in the maternal-feminist sources, and nothing in their child-welfare focus implies a taxation view.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic; Key's state pay for mothers is related but conditional on motherhood, not unconditional.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Prairie maternalists were farm-focused, but none of the sources links motherhood-based claims to tariff policy, so adherents are left split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a social-protection rather than industrial-policy focus.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Prairie farm-family reformers might like small holdings, but the sources do not tie the maternal case to property distribution.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Only fringe socialist voices would agree; Key and Addams work within wage society.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions fall outside the movement's concerns, which centre on votes, health, temperance and child welfare.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not a documented position; inferred from reliance on the ballot and civic organisations.

one-party-rule.rationale: The movement's central campaign was for votes and democratic participation (McClung, Addams).

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Canadian and British adherents lived under monarchy without making it an issue; Lady Aberdeen was a viceroy's wife.

democracy-best.rationale: Their aim was women's inclusion in democracy; McClung calls it failing when people lack a voice.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed beyond suffrage; prairie reformers did favour some direct legislation, not documented here.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred from preference for the ballot and parliaments.

right-to-secede.rationale: Regional secession was never part of maternal feminism's suffrage and welfare agenda; no view can be inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: They argued women are equally fit for public life, rejecting claims that some are naturally ruling.

political-violence-never.rationale: Pacifism was a natural link (Stowe-Gullen); McClung condemns war and militarism.

war-builds-character.rationale: McClung calls war a human failure and attacks militarism's effect on children and the church.

separate-church-state.rationale: Evangelical activists wanted moral legislation (prohibition); not a stated church-state theory.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Faith inspired their reforms, but they argued from welfare not scripture as law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: They looked to public institutions for protection and reform.

military-superiority.rationale: Pacifist current and McClung's attack on militarism cut against arms superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Race-of-the-nation rhetoric in imperial strands, yet Addams embraces immigrants; split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Key says the struggle cannot be sex against sex but class against class, yet mainstream maternal feminists stressed moral cooperation, not conflict as history's engine.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred: they asked a 'fair deal' and equal chances for women, not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Documented as excluding Indigenous women; no support known.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Imperial outlook of many adherents; no support documented.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from imperial-nationalist framing of many adherents.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Their politics rests on care, duty to others and service; McClung calls charity and love the banner.

duties-before-rights.rationale: They stressed women's duties of care but claimed rights too; split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Valuing nature for itself belongs to later environmental thought; the motherhood-centred movement left it unaddressed.

limit-population.rationale: Pro-natal 'mothers of the race' concern about the birth rate opposes limiting population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: They reformed industrial cities rather than rejecting them.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Their reform case relies on public regulation of existing conditions (Addams), not on speeding technological change, so no lean follows.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from eugenic-moral outlook and emphasis on natural motherhood.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The question postdates the movement by a century, and nothing in its reliance on human civic participation suggests an answer.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A digital-era issue with no analogue in the movement's sources, so no stance is inferable.

restore-past-order.rationale: They wanted reform, though with conservative framing of motherhood.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Reformers like Addams argue from concrete conditions in homes and cities, yet the movement was driven by a moral doctrine of motherhood; the sources do not settle it.

direct-action.rationale: They used petition, ballot and organisation (WCTU, NCW), not direct action; militants of suffrage came from other strands.

means-match-ends.rationale: McClung's insistence on love and a fair deal suggests means should fit ends; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: They sought better urban and domestic conditions, not a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: They valued women's distinct caring role; Key says each sex should keep its strengths.

production-for-use.rationale: Only the socialist wing (Richardson, Henderson) might phrase economics this way; the mainstream sources do not discuss production aims.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Socialist maternal feminists would agree; liberal ones not.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Incompatible with their ballot-based democratic politics.

collective-farming.rationale: Prairie reformers were farm-family oriented; collectivisation not documented.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Pacifists blamed militarism rather than capitalism; socialists dissent.

taxation-theft.rationale: They sought public services funded collectively (sanitation, schools, health).

harm-principle.rationale: Moral reformers restricted behaviour beyond harm to others, but the case for prohibition was harm-based; split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Their case rests on mothers and children as social groups with needs; inferred.

conscription.rationale: Many maternal feminists were pacifists before 1914 and expected women's votes to end war, but in Canada and elsewhere the movement divided over wartime conscription in 1917, so the lean against is weak.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Voice via the ballot was their central demand.

state-as-business.rationale: Addams says a city is 'enlarged housekeeping' as well as a business corporation, and treats citizens as members.

positive-liberty.rationale: Addams argues that women lack the means to protect their homes without public action, so freedom needs material conditions.

media-academia-power.rationale: The movement used the press for campaigns but never made a claim about universities and media outranking officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Eugenic and racial ideas were present in some strands, but the movement had no collective doctrine on this.

organic-representation.rationale: Women's clubs and councils were organised representation, but the movement sought party-electoral votes.

total-state.rationale: Opposed by their liberal-reform and democratic outlook.

national-rebirth.rationale: Imperial 'mothers of the race' language implies renewal of the nation; mixed with reform framing.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Imperial sentiment existed, but pacifism cut against expansion by force.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Entirely at odds with their democratic suffrage agenda.

bound-labor.rationale: They defended working women and children's labor protection (Addams).

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; philosophy of knowledge was not their concern.

universal-morality.rationale: Evangelical moral reformers assumed shared moral truths; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Municipal housekeeping suggests a common good, but Addams says all points of view must be represented.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zionism was not a maternal-feminist question, and no source for this movement takes a side.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights were outside the movement's agenda, which focused on women's status within existing states.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival was not among their causes; the Canadian movement existed in English and French strands without a shared line.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workplace voting rights appear only in socialist offshoots, not in the mainstream maternalist texts read.

school-vouchers.rationale: Addams wants better public schools with women's say; vouchers not discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Budget policy is absent from the sources; adherents wanted services funded but did not argue about deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Their case for public protection of homes cuts against economic-liberty-first claims.

rule-by-example.rationale: They wanted laws such as child-labor and sanitation regulation, not rule by moral example alone.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement sought women's rights within empire and nation states and did not theorise national self-determination.

force-without-un.rationale: The UN postdates the movement; the sources' pacifism points mildly against unilateral force, but it is an inference.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Evangelical Protestantism was central; moral feeling and motherhood were valued alongside reason.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Addams extends services to immigrant families; other strands were racially exclusive.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Mothers' pensions aimed to let mothers stay home and care; Key wants state pay for motherhood years.

class-collaboration.rationale: Upper-class women organised to help poorer women and sought moral cooperation over class war.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not their position; they valued institutions of education and culture.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: They wanted women in public life and politics on equal political terms, even while arguing they had distinct strengths; law should not assign roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury laws were not a maternal-feminist campaign; the sources say nothing on lending.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Racism existed among adherents, but legal segregation was not their program; inferred.

state-class-instrument.rationale: They used the state as a tool for reform, not as a class instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: An energy-policy question that postdates the movement, so no position can be derived from the sources.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Wikipedia links the movement to racial undertones on immigrants, while Addams values immigrant customs; split.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claim not part of their program.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral-system design was not discussed; their demand was the franchise itself.

national-mission.rationale: Imperial missions appear in strands, but unsettled.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: McClung and Key criticise laws resting on paternal right and denying women a voice, but mostly framed as unfairness rather than structure.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: McClung says women are needed to clean up political corruption, especially the liquor trade's electoral influence.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics concerns linked to the movement (Wikipedia), though not all adherents agreed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: They sought active government in health, food, schools and housing.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial undertones in some strands; no documented stance on this.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Women's claim was equal moral and civic worth, though racial exclusion limited it in practice.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A debate internal to Marxism; socialist maternal feminists are mentioned only briefly in the sources.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler-state adherents in Canada did not hold this view.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law debates in plural religious societies were not a maternal-feminist subject in the sources.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religious conversion law was outside the movement's agenda, though it was evangelical Protestant in tone.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Evangelical motivation suggests acceptance of religion in schools; low confidence.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Women demanded the ballot as consent; Addams calls it the implement for self-government.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist balance-of-trade aims are not discussed in any of the movement's sources.

population-transfer.rationale: Not a documented position; contradicts reformist ethics.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Pacifists agree on war but not on property-based framing.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: McClung's banner is love and a fair deal; they emphasised cooperation and care.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The sources do not discuss banning parties; their own campaign was to enter party politics.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Addams and McClung object to women's dependence on others' influence and favour direct equal votes; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design beyond the vote is not discussed, though the Persons case went through courts.

vanguard-party.rationale: Reform through mass organisation and the ballot, not vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Settlement houses and clubs helped poor women and children; McClung looks to root causes of poverty.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A late-twentieth-century British housing policy; the movement's tenement concerns (Addams) concerned inspection, not tenant purchase.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is absent from the sources; adherents' stance on labor conflict was reformist and varied.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: McClung locates poverty in unjust laws and the liquor trade rather than population.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Their demand was to vote and stand for office, so selecting officials by lot is not something the sources raise.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from their rights-claiming and civic outlook.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Addams wants food inspection, not price control.

party-controls-media.rationale: They campaigned through free press and public speech.

party-commands-army.rationale: Incompatible with their democratic, pacifist outlook.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not covered; Addams defends immigrant participation while other strands had racial undertones.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of legislators was not discussed in these sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party discipline is a question of organisation the movement's sources do not take up.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational union is a late-twentieth-century question; the sources give no basis for inferring an answer.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; Protestant reformers of varied church orders.

clerical-rule.rationale: Women sought political voice for lay people including women, which a clerical government would deny.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Pacifism was hard to hold during WWI (Wikipedia), and most supported their countries' war effort.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral-purity reformers favoured regulating morals laws; Wikipedia lists morality laws among concerns.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term rules for presidents were not part of a movement living under parliamentary monarchy and US/Canadian practice.

recall-officials.rationale: Prairie reformers favoured recall, not documented in sources read.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not discussed; only a vague pacifism is on record.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Addams wants tenement inspection, accepting rented homes. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Prairie strands idealised farm families, yet urban reformers worked in cities; split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Partition and reunification were not issues for the movement's sources.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: They valued education and women's learning (McClung).

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Moral purity reformers favoured some sex education, but gender equality was framed differently; split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Evolution teaching was not a stated maternalist cause; Addams asks for broader curricula without addressing it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Moral-reform strands pursued morality laws against indecency, and Addams and others targeted exploitation.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not covered; the Persons case concerned women as 'persons', not descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language support in schools is not discussed; Francophone maternal feminists existed separately in Quebec.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The movement's sources do not take up exemptions from general laws for religious minorities.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Moral reformers favoured respectable norms; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt is outside the movement's concerns and period.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-colonial economics is not part of the movement; adherents largely accepted empire.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Rewriting constitutions was not their goal; they sought inclusion in the existing ones.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Opposite of their freedom-seeking, suffrage case. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Missionary and charitable impulses existed, but McClung criticised charity that does not reach root causes.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the movement; its pacifist current suggests mild opposition at most.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Presidential selection is not discussed; adherents lived in monarchy or federal republic without taking a line.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking is not a subject in the maternal-feminist sources.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Addams justifies regulation of housing and sweatshops for the common good of homes.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist-debate question that the movement, which mostly ended before or around the Russian Revolution, never addressed.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Public-health and food inspection reasoning suggests acting before harm; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Pacifists would be wary of mutual war guarantees.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Lady Aberdeen and other adherents lived under a ceremonial crown, but no source states a view on its role.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Secession is not discussed, so no stance on using force follows.

region-keeps-system.rationale: One-country-two-systems arrangements are unrelated to the movement's agenda.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from social-reform goals; not addressed.

character-from-environment.rationale: Addams shows how tenements, sanitation and schools shape families and children.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Opposed by their rights-claiming constitutional case (Persons case).

space-expansion.rationale: Spaceflight lies far outside the movement's period and concerns.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical theory of mixed government does not appear in the sources.

equal-parenting.rationale: Anachronistic; maternal feminism treated mothers as primary carers but also supported child welfare.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate with no connection to the maternal-feminist sources.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are not covered by the movement's sources.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Incompatible with their liberal-reform outlook. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

women-must-cover.rationale: They sought women's public participation and a fair deal. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not mentioned in the sources.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic unions were not a maternal-feminist cause.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Austro-Marxist minority autonomy was not on their agenda.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Addams stresses immigrant civic participation where they live; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Addams stresses conditions, McClung stresses moral choice; split.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is not discussed, though Addams accepts regulation of business generally.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm rescues are not discussed in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Persons case used courts to win women's rights; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Maternal feminists wanted women in office, but parity quotas are anachronistic; split.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-linked standards are not discussed, though labor protection for women and girls (Addams) was favoured.

moral-incentives.rationale: Incentive structures at work are not addressed; the sources concern votes and welfare.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Opposite of their pacifist reform method. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Titles were a matter of course in the British Empire, and sources (Lady Aberdeen led the NCW) give no indication of campaigns against them.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Curricular emphasis on national history is not addressed; Addams only asks that schools teach more than the three R's.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Imperial maternal feminists supported it; others did not.

patriotic-education.rationale: Patriotism in schools is not discussed; McClung's critique of militarism in children's education suggests partial doubt, but adherents differ.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: A late-twentieth-century affirmative-action debate with no counterpart in the movement's sources.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not part of the movement's program.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The sources do not discuss capitalism's crises; only the socialist strand would take a side.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperial loyalty common among adherents; no consistent position.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory remedies are unrelated to the movement's sources.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis not found in the maternal-feminist sources.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Opposite of their equal-treatment claims for women. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Persons case (1929) used constitutional interpretation, but the sources do not state a view on entrenched bills of rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial boundary treaties were not a maternal-feminist subject.

elective-rulers.rationale: They sought equal participation in elections.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Right-of-resistance theory is not discussed; the movement worked by petition and vote.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary supremacy is not directly discussed, though they sought votes for parliaments.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Compassion for the vulnerable fits the ethic, but animal welfare is not documented in these sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Upper-class women organised settlements and clubs to help poorer women, sometimes with a reforming condescension.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Opposite: McClung says politics is everyone's business.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt-school critique of mass culture does not appear in the movement's sources.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is a later theory and not in the sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-systems theory is a later Marxist development unrelated to the sources.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for native-born citizens is not a stated position; Addams defends immigrant civic participation while others had nativist undertones.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist-party independence is irrelevant to the sources read.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development aid is a postwar concern; the movement had no stated position.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Pacifist adherents such as McClung condemn war as a human failure, so fighting to recover lost land is inferred as disfavoured.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not supported; Indigenous women were excluded in practice.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Fascism emerged after the movement's peak, so there is no stated position.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The comparison of fascism and communism postdates the movement.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A historiographic dispute not addressed in the sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: A modern monuments debate with no equivalent in the movement.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's disadvantage programmes are a late-twentieth-century issue; the movement focused on women's and children's needs.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Maternal feminists focused on protecting women and children from men; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Civilizational relativism about institutions is not in the sources.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Opposite of pacifist and civilian-democratic outlook. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

paid-care-work.rationale: Key proposes that the state remunerate women during the years when motherhood is their vocation; maternalists treated care as society's most important work.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign ownership of strategic firms is not discussed.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Key defended freer divorce, while Protestant moralists resisted; split.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandate is not part of maternal-feminist thought as documented.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Occupancy-based land tenure was not part of their agenda.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The sources do not discuss parliamentary control of budgets, though they demanded the vote that selects parliaments.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is not discussed; Canadian adherents operated in English and French settings.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land ownership by foreigners is not addressed by the sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate-impact doctrine is a modern legal concept outside the sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Moral reformers disliked luxury and display; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Opposite of pacifism. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

corporate-influence.rationale: McClung attacks the liquor trade's corrupting influence over elections.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign funding of NGOs is a recent issue; the sources are silent.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Concern for birth rate and 'mothers of the race' supported encouraging families; Key also backs state support for mothers.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local residency limits on home purchases are not discussed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employer-of-last-resort proposals are not part of the sources, which concern mothers' support and working conditions.

democratic-peace.rationale: Pacifists expected women's vote to bring peace; spread of democracy implied.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: They worked through law and the vote; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: The sources show pacifism but no view on sovereignty or non-interference doctrine.

industrial-unions.rationale: Craft versus industrial unionism is not discussed in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy theories about minorities are not part of the movement's program, and the sources show none.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: They valued marriage as partnership (McClung) and legal reform of it, not abolition.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom of information laws are not discussed.

local-production.rationale: Local-economy ideals are not in the sources.

informal-organisation.rationale: They organised through formal councils, unions and clubs.

national-law-over-international.rationale: International courts postdate the movement; no view documented.

religious-nation.rationale: Defining the nation by religion is not stated, even though evangelical Protestantism shaped adherents.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary diplomacy is not part of any maternal-feminist source.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Communist property doctrine is not part of the mainstream movement.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cold War anti-communism postdates the movement.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service delivery mixes are not discussed; Addams assumes city provision of basics.

religion-illusion.rationale: Evangelical faith was central to the movement.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Assessments of capitalism's historical role are not in the sources.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Socialist maternal feminists and Key say yes; liberal ones do not.

socialized-care.rationale: They treated mothers' own care as central, though Key supports state remuneration, not replacement of mothers.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaty obligations toward nations within borders are not covered in the sources, and the movement ignored Indigenous claims.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Utopian commune ideals are not part of the sources.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settlement policy for majority groups is not in the sources, though race-of-the-nation talk existed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third-position doctrines are not part of the sources; the movement was reformist inside capitalism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historic homeland claims are not discussed.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not a position of the movement. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anachronistic; period moral norms vs. no documented campaign.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Contradicts their reliance on public persuasion and the ballot.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Blasphemy law is not covered in the sources, though adherents were often evangelical.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not addressed; imperial loyalty without such doctrine.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The duty is specific to Islamic law and no maternal-feminist source addresses armed religious obligation.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Opposite of their peaceful, democratic method.

participatory-democracy.rationale: McClung and Addams want ordinary women taking part directly in public decisions.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Documented as excluding women of color and working-class women rather than analysing intersection. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Legal gender identity recognition is a recent issue; the movement predates it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Assisted dying is not discussed in the sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Whether left-right is outdated is not discussed.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Islam is not discussed in the sources.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Evangelicals split on divine authority versus popular consent; McClung reads faith as a call to act.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress in state institutions is not discussed.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from protective stance on women.

social-market-economy.rationale: Closest fit among economic frameworks: market with social protection for mothers and children.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Pacifists such as Stowe-Gullen hoped to end war; abolition not explicit.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary leadership is not addressed in the sources.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist banking is not part of the sources.

property-franchise.rationale: They demanded votes irrespective of sex, and had little regard for property tests.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Anachronistic; ecofeminist thesis not part of this movement.

reification.rationale: A Marxist philosophical concept absent from the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Critique of press ownership is not part of the sources.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rights claims within law (Persons case); inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: The movement was racially exclusionary in practice but did not propose racial franchise; contradicts women's claims of vote on equal terms.

online-participation.rationale: Internet deliberation postdates the movement by a century.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Religious intermarriage limits are not in the sources.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are a recent idea; the movement sought elected office.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Boycotts of minority-owned shops are not part of the movement's program and the sources show none.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: McClung reinterprets 'Thy will be done' as a call to act against injustice.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The sources do not state this argument, though Addams stresses dependence on public services.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: A late-twentieth-century issue outside the sources.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Evangelical movement. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Reformers wanted protection and prison reform, not abolition. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociationalism is a later theory not found in the sources.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: McClung says charity merely smoothes things over without reaching root causes; Addams relies on city action.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is a recent proposal absent from the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction-risk concern is a modern question outside the sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Movements split; many church-based women's groups still barred women leaders.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: McClung calls marriage a 'divine partnership' and Key criticises family law resting on paternal right.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; Addams argues immigrant women's concerns need voices.

rent-control.rationale: Rent caps are not discussed, although Addams wants housing standards enforced on landlords.

abolish-ip.rationale: Patents and copyrights are not discussed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: McClung warns of militarism shaping children.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the movement; the pacifist current suggests mild support.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Basing agreements are not discussed in the sources.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Genocide recognition is a late-twentieth-century issue.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Income from property versus work is not discussed outside the socialist strand.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Nation-continuity myths are not part of the sources.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Held that women's nature and mothering are real and distinct. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: McClung criticises militarism and war glorification.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Their politics rested on the category of women as mothers and caregivers. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Evangelical moral crusades suggest partial; not documented.

culture-before-state.rationale: Cultural nationalism is not part of these sources.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; McClung critiques the church.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist theology postdates the movement; McClung reinterprets verses to support action, but no general test is stated.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Ethnic economic nationalism is not in the sources.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Ethnic administrative unification is not in the sources.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from support for working women; not documented.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Addams ties water, sanitation, inspection and food safety to city government.

second-chamber.rationale: The Persons case concerned Senate access, but no stance on second chambers.

municipal-property.rationale: Not addressed beyond municipal housekeeping of services.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Municipal confederalism is a later libertarian-municipalist idea not in the sources.

family-wage.rationale: Key says mothers working in factories leave homes without time; the male-earner home was assumed by many maternalists.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Public protection mindset leans toward caution; inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Longevity research funding is a modern issue.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Cryptographic payment privacy is a modern issue.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online pseudonymity is a modern issue.

person-over-state.rationale: Personalist philosophy is not part of the sources.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Evangelical Protestantism central; Key sees motherhood as spiritual development.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Regional autonomy rules are not discussed.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Racial exclusion present; no such doctrine in the sources.

racial-pride.rationale: Imperial race-pride language in strands; not systematic.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Pacifist tendency and McClung's attack on war favour defensive-only war.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Linguistic nationalism is not part of these sources.

communal-electorates.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from universal suffrage claim.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Conspiracy claims about partition are not part of the movement's program and the sources show none.

free-public-college.rationale: Tuition policy is not discussed, though they wanted women's education broadened.

future-generations.rationale: Children and the race's future were central to the movement's reasoning.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Maternal feminists held that women's role as mothers gave them distinct nurturing values that should count in politics; McClung and Addams argue women's view is needed.

arms-reduction.rationale: McClung condemns militarism and Stowe-Gullen expected women to end war.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital flow controls are not discussed.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Disarming non-state groups is not discussed.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Pacifists vs. war supporters split in WWI.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from reform of working conditions; not documented.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits for low-paid families postdate the movement.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Statutory borrowing limits are not discussed.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: New international economic order claims are postwar.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Opposite of their reform of existing government.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Economic pluralism between communities is not discussed.

sacred-nation.rationale: Sacralised nationhood is not part of the sources.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Internal-colonialism theory is not part of the sources.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from belief in essential sex nature; fits fixed nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Public broadcasting postdates most of the movement.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Perennialism is not part of the sources.

farm-price-support.rationale: Prairie reformers in Grain Growers movement favoured it, but not documented.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the movement; pacifist inference leans against.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from protective stance toward women and girls.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal legal rights, including property, were part of women's claim to a fair deal; Key notes family law still rests on paternal right.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Language-naming disputes are not in the sources.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Role for customary chiefs is not discussed.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environmental priority over liberty is not discussed.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Sentencing law is not discussed beyond gesture to prison reform.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Language tests for immigrants are not discussed; Addams champions immigrant women.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from support for worker organisation.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Equal legal recognition of interpretations is not discussed.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The sources do not define democracy procedurally; they want votes plus substantive reform.

premarital-sex.rationale: Moral-purity reformers (WCTU, Pappritz) held a single standard of chastity; Key dissents, so low-medium.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; opposed to suppression of speech.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Negative income tax is a postwar idea not discussed in the sources.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western fronts are a postcolonial idea; imperial-loyal adherents would reject it but the sources give no position.

workers-nation.rationale: Whether workers organise nationally or internationally is not discussed, except that socialist maternal feminists were pacifist internationalists.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from the movement's moral-reform stress on justice and protection of the vulnerable; the sources do not discuss past state killings.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Some strands held racial and imperial views while Addams celebrates immigrant neighbours, so adherents are split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Imperial adherents ranked civilisations while Addams respects immigrant customs; the sources show a split.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation law is not discussed in the maternal-feminist sources.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from pacifism and McClung's critique of militarism; great-power bloc discipline is not discussed.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Tort-based pollution remedies are a libertarian theory the sources never touch; Addams prefers public inspection.

women-suffrage.rationale: Votes for women is the central demand of the movement: Addams calls the ballot the implement women need to protect the home and McClung demands a fair deal.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Many maternal feminists were evangelical and drew their mission from Christian duty and the WCTU, so they saw religion as support for women's public role.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: the movement predates modern race science critiques, and some strands used 'mothers of the race' language that treated race as a real group.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: maternal feminists pushed the state to create public health, child welfare and maternal protection services, which suggests support for state bodies serving women, though not gender-equality agencies as such.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The movement did not address how property is first acquired, and strands ran from socialist to settler-minded, so adherents are split.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from Addams-style pacifism and the movement's moral internationalism; international criminal courts post-date it.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Many strands were evangelical but others were reformist or socialist, so adherents are split on literal readings of scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: a movement built on women's right to public participation would want it included in any self-government; the sources do not discuss it.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Anachronistic: inferred from the movement's reform-through-democracy outlook, which does not fit a bureaucratic planned state.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: the movement's central demand was the direct ballot for women, so it favoured voters electing offices directly.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred: many strands were Protestant and temperance churchwomen, but others favoured plural religious standing, so adherents are split.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and imperial 'mothers of the race' strands differ from internationalist ones, so adherents are split.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are split between pacifist self-determination and imperial strands.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: imperial strands accepted colonial rule while pacifist strands did not, so the question splits adherents.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: domestic thrift sat alongside support for modern public health and sanitation, so adherents are split.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the prairie movement was largely settler-based and welcomed settlement, though Indigenous questions were seldom raised in the sources.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: the movement stressed sex differences and mothers' distinct duties, so a draft covering women was unlikely to be sought.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from the 'mothers of the race' and imperial strands that tied motherhood to national duty.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from the movement's moral reform and temperance aims and its sanctity-of-life framing; drugs were alcohol-focused.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed; anachronistic for the period.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Not addressed; imperial and nationalist strands existed but no position is documented.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its duty-centred view of women's role as mothers and moral guardians over an individualist rights claim.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from campaigns for mothers' pensions and aid to poor mothers and children, which were targeted.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: the movement worked through women's organisations such as the WCTU and lobbied parties rather than bypassing them.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from municipal-housekeeping reform against graft and special interests such as the liquor trade.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Many strands were evangelical and drew on Protestant moral reform in public life.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from its blend of progressive reform with traditional family-centred roles.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred: strands split between protecting wives from bad husbands and defending marriage.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement's racial attitudes ranged from inclusion to eugenic racism.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from the evangelical moral-authority framing and McClung's appeal to a higher justice.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its family and work-ethic orientation.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from Addams's pairing of civic patriotism with concern for working people, especially women and children.

material-over-identity.rationale: Not addressed; the movement combined welfare concerns with a gendered moral identity.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from the movement's Christian reformist and democratic character, which was opposed to communist rule.

missingStatements.text: Women should have the same right as men to vote and hold public office.
missingStatements.rationale: Votes for women is the central demand of the movement: Addams calls the ballot the implement women need to protect the home and McClung demands a fair deal.

missingStatements.text: The sale of alcohol should be prohibited by law.
missingStatements.rationale: Temperance and prohibition were core maternal-feminist causes, tied to the WCTU, and McClung says women bear the liquor trade's costs without choosing it.
missingStatements.declined: Single-issue temperance claim; legalize-drugs and laws-from-scripture capture the nearby positions, and it would be answered by every audit for little signal.

notes: The strand is internally varied: socialist maternal feminists (Richardson, Henderson) and pacifists differ from evangelical, eugenic and imperial strands, so many economic and nationalism answers are split or inferred. Many answers are low-confidence inferences from a movement that mostly campaigned on suffrage, temperance and child welfare. McClung read only through roughly the first third of the book, Key through the first part.
